segments.text: Episode seventy-six. Season five: the explorers. Next stop... the Hubble Space Telescope.
On April twenty-fourth, nineteen ninety, the space shuttle Discovery carried the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit.
segments.headline: Launched, 1990

segments.text: Above the blurring of Earth's air, it would see the universe more sharply than ever. But the first pictures came back blurry.
segments.headline: Blurry pictures

segments.text: Its main mirror had been ground to the wrong shape, off by about a fiftieth of the width of a human hair.
Jokes about the expensive mistake were everywhere. But NASA had a plan: Hubble was built to be repaired by astronauts.
segments.headline: Built to be repaired

segments.text: In nineteen ninety-three, astronauts added corrective optics. Glasses, for a telescope. The images became stunning.
segments.headline: Glasses for a telescope

segments.text: Five servicing missions kept it upgraded. The last one flew in two thousand nine.
Hubble helped measure the age of the universe, showed that its expansion is speeding up, and photographed galaxies billions of light-years away.
segments.headline: What Hubble found

segments.text: Thirty-six years later, despite aging gyroscopes, it's still working, and NASA expects it to continue into the twenty-thirties.
segments.headline: Still working
